intent: Give the user a tested toolkit ready for the day a Ulefone Armor X12 Pro arrives: a host-readiness gate, a read-only recon script that decides which rooting path applies, a MediaTek-only stock partition dump, and post-flash verification. Everything testable without the device is validated against a Pixel 6a read-only, and everything that is not is labelled as such.
scope: Non-goal: any flashing script; irreversible partition writes stay manual and deliberate
Non-goal: any write to the Pixel 6a, which is the user's daily driver
Non-goal: modifying root_bl9000.sh, which still serves a different device
Binary artifacts live in ~/.cache/mtk-root/, never in the repo
changes: Added lib/mtk_common.sh with two device-read seams (dev_getprop, dev_list_by_name) that read from fixture files when MTK_ROOT_FIXTURE is set, making the whole suite offline and hermetic

discover_partitions derives the slot scheme from observed _a suffixes and selects the ramdisk carrier by preference order init_boot then boot over the partitions actually present, never hardcoding either name; the AOSP launch-version rule explains the ordering but the code reads the filesystem

classify_device requires a positive MediaTek platform signal AND a vendor match for ULEFONE, with no 'not a Pixel therefore Ulefone' fallback, so an unrecognised third device lands in UNKNOWN and every caller refuses
10-recon.sh triages unauthorized-versus-device before any getprop, because an unauthorized device returns empty properties that would otherwise be misreported as 'device has no properties'

Carrier lock is hardcoded to UNDETERMINED with the raw signals printed, since sys.oem_unlock_allowed, ro.oem_unlock_supported and settings global oem_unlock_allowed all read identically whether a device is carrier-locked or merely has the toggle off

20-dump-stock.sh reads the ramdisk partition name from the recon facts file rather than re-deriving it, so a dump can only ever target a partition already seen in a recon report; MTK_DUMP_CMD stubs the mtkclient call for tests
90-verify-root.sh reports each check independently with no aggregate verdict, since partial root is a real state and which part failed is the useful information
Added udev/60-mtk-root.rules scoped to Google 18d1 and MediaTek 0e8d using MODE=0660 plus TAG+=uaccess instead of world-writable 0666

install.sh clones mtkclient fresh, rebuilds its venv when it cannot import its dependencies, and gates the catch-all udev repair behind --fix-udev with a timestamped backup rather than rewriting another script's file silently
Fixed a SIGPIPE abort in 00-preflight.sh where 'adb version | head -1' under pipefail exited 141 and killed the script mid-run
Fixed a silent exit in 20-dump-stock.sh where find on a nonexistent cache dir failed under set -e, so the script printed its title and stopped without explaining that recon must run first

Fixed a hole in the read-only static scan: stripping all quoted strings to avoid false positives on printf text also hid mtk_adb shell "reboot bootloader" from every check; now only printf/echo/cat arguments are stripped, and a negative self-test asserts the scan fails on injected commands

verification.evidence: 58 passed, 0 failed. Includes: selects init_boot_a over co-present boot_a; A-only bare names; falls back to boot_a on the Pixel fixture; UNKNOWN device exits 1 with no PATH claimed; dump refuses a Pixel; dump manifest records sha256, size and idempotence; a 512-byte dump is rejected as implausibly small; scan catches injected 'adb shell "reboot bootloader"', bare fastboot, and settings put.

12 passed, 0 failed, 0 warnings -- HOST READY. adb 1.0.41, fastboot 37.0.0, python3 3.14.6, git 2.55.0, sha256sum 9.11; plugdev and adbusers active; 60-mtk-root.rules present and udevadm verify clean; no world-writable catch-all; mtkclient venv importable; mtkclient rev 0542a87; cache dir writable.

Reported: classified as PIXEL; A/B scheme A/B; slot suffix _a; ramdisk lives in boot -> partition boot_a; 'Magisk must patch BOOT on this device (no init_boot present)'; flash.locked=1, verifiedbootstate=green; OEM-unlock toggle UNREADABLE; Carrier lock UNDETERMINED; decision 'PATH C or D (Pixel) - INDETERMINATE' with a refusal to act. Device state after the run was unchanged: flash.locked=1, verifiedbootstate=green, 53 partitions visible, adb state 'device'.

verification.command: negative test: inject 'mtk_adb shell "reboot bootloader"' into a copy of 10-recon.sh and run the read-only scan
verification.evidence: Before the fix the injected command was NOT CAUGHT, confirming the guard had been weakened by the quote-stripping. After the fix all three injections (quoted adb reboot, bare fastboot, settings put) are detected, and the unmodified script still yields no findings.

Cloned mtkclient fresh at rev 0542a87 (2026-08-02) and built a venv under Python 3.14.6 that imports cleanly. The pre-existing venv at ~/.cache/bl9000-root/mtkclient failed the same import with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'usb', which is the breakage 00-preflight.sh now detects.
1 udev rules files have been checked. Success: 1, Fail: 0.

Commented the world-writable catch-all in /etc/udev/rules.d/51-android.rules with backup 51-android.rules.bak-20260804T183038Z. Afterwards adb still lists 23181JEGR08034 as 'device', 'udevadm test' no longer applies any wildcard rule, and no active uncommented idVendor=="*" rule remains.

verification.command: shellcheck (no severity filter) over all new shell files
verification.evidence: mtk_common.sh, install.sh, 00-preflight.sh, 10-recon.sh, 20-dump-stock.sh, 90-verify-root.sh and tests/run_tests.sh all report zero findings. Two SC2034 findings on unused size constants were resolved by adding the mtk_sane_ramdisk_size function that consumes them, not by suppression.

risks: The Ulefone launched on Android 13, so it most likely carries the ramdisk in init_boot -- the opposite branch from the Pixel used for validation. The init_boot selection path is proven by fixtures only and has never run against hardware that has that partition.

Ulefone property values (manufacturer, model, ro.board.platform) are guessed. If the real unit reports something outside the patterns, classify_device returns UNKNOWN and every script refuses. This fails safe but will resemble a bug on first contact; --explain-classification and a single marked pattern block in mtk_common.sh are the intended remedy.

Path semantics A/B/C/D are inferred because the companion document defining them was never provided; 10-recon.sh prints an assumption banner on every run rather than presenting the mapping as authoritative.

mtkclient reading a real partition over BROM is untested. Chipset support exists (rev 0542a87 has an MT6765 entry with an mt6765_payload.bin loader) but this unit's SLA/DAA authentication state is undocumented and per-device.
udev rules are syntactically verified and adb access is confirmed for a Google VID, but access to a MediaTek device in BROM mode cannot be confirmed without the hardware.

Commenting the catch-all udev rule narrows USB permissions system-wide. adb was re-verified afterwards, but a device that relied on the wildcard rule and is not covered by 18d1 or 0e8d would need its VID added.
The Magisk release publishes both Magisk-v30.7.apk and a 25 MB app-debug.apk; selecting the wrong asset is an easy error, recorded in NOTES.md and stock/README.md.
rollback: git revert the commit: the toolkit is self-contained under linux_configuration/scripts/mtk_root/ plus lib/mtk_common.sh, and no existing script imports either.

Restore the udev catch-all if needed: sudo cp -a /etc/udev/rules.d/51-android.rules.bak-20260804T183038Z /etc/udev/rules.d/51-android.rules && sudo udevadm control --reload-rules && sudo udevadm trigger
Remove the narrowed rules with sudo rm /etc/udev/rules.d/60-mtk-root.rules followed by a udevadm reload, and delete ~/.cache/mtk-root/ to discard the clone, venv and downloaded APK.

After any rollback, confirm 'adb devices' still lists the phone as 'device' and that root_bl9000.sh's own udev expectations (Google 18d1, MediaTek 0e8d) remain satisfied by /etc/udev/rules.d/51-android.rules.
